messages:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to decompose the 'request-ferry' monolith into two pieces: a thin, stateless ferry-proxy (hotpath routing/auth/throttling) and a stateful cargo-sidecar (enrichment, durable checkpoints).

maya: Short RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/31876-decompose-ferry — TL;DR in this thread.

maya: Motivation: reduce hotpath p99 variance and make deployment surface smaller for batching/quantization experiments. Baseline on ferry: p95 ~120ms, p99 ~340ms.

raj: Question — where does the KV ownership live after split? cargo-sidecar or a shared store?

maya: Two options sketched in RFC:
- Plan A: cargo-sidecar owns sticky-session KV and exposes a low-latency cache API.
- Plan B: extract a thin storage API (storage-service) and keep ownership central.
Tradeoff: A = lowest latency but more cross-tenant coordination; B = simpler ownership but extra hop.

sam: Observability note — we must guarantee trace propagation across both services. If spans get lost we'll lose p99 signal. Need a clear span contract.

lia: Also: cargo-sidecar will hold secrets and ML feature materializations. It must live in private subnets with KMS access. ferry-proxy stays in public subnets.

alex: Rollout question — can we canary by routing 5% to the new pair while keeping the monolith? How are we avoiding double side-effects on writes?

maya: Rollout plan: shadow writes to cargo-sidecar for 2w, no commit to durable paths until checksum diff matches. We'll run side-by-side diffs.

erin: SDK compatibility: surface must be identical for callers. Proxy should handle discovery so client SDKs don't need changes.

raj: Testing: we need to replay production traces through both paths. I can adapt the trace-replayer to produce diffs. ETA ~2w.

sam: Risk: cache warmup could spike load. Mitigation: prefill caches at ramp and incremental traffic percentage. Also add backpressure at proxy-level.

maya: Proposed phasing (short):
1) infra & network prep + KMS placement
2) cargo-sidecar feature parity tests (integration)
3) shadow mode + diff run (2w)
4) incremental canary (5% -> 25% -> 50%) with rollback gates
5) flip feature flag and deprecate old path

alex: Add escape hatch: route heavy/unknown requests back to monolith if p99 latency worsens >20% for 10m. Put that in runbook.

sam: I'll draft span contract and dashboard widgets: ferry.latency.p95/p99, cargo.calls.count, crossservice.error.delta, sidecar.diff.mismatch_rate.

maya: Action items (owners & dates):
- raj: replay harness + migration testcases (due 2025-01-15)
- sam: tracing & span contract doc + dashboards (due 2025-01-08)
- lia: network placement + KMS + subnet plan (due 2024-12-20)
- alex: rollout runbook (canary steps + rollback + escape hatch) (due 2025-01-10)
- erin: SDK compatibility signoff (by 2025-01-05)

raj: I will also add a smoke test suite that fails the canary if any checksum diffs > 0.1% across sample traces.

lia: Network note — cargo-sidecars should be scheduled on nodes with local NVMe to support checkpointing; I'll draft constraint SLO for placement.

erin: SDK folks will provide a compatibility shim in the next minor release, no consumer changes expected.

alex: I'm volunteering to be rollout owner for canary and final flip.

maya: Great. If we confirm owners I'll open the RFC PR with the phase plan and risk table.

deploy-bot: Scheduled deployment window opened: 2025-01-12 02:00 UTC — reserve if needed.

maya: Thanks all — I’ll draft the RFC PR later today. If anyone sees a hard blocker DM me. :thumbsup:
